specification: Implement an order state machine with payment retries and a return window in the package orders. orders/errors.py (read-only, already provided) defines TransitionError and its subclasses InvalidTransition(state, event), RetryTooEarly(retry_at) and ReturnWindowClosed(deadline), each storing its constructor arguments as attributes of the same names. orders/states.py holds the static life-cycle data and helpers; orders/machine.py defines the class Order; orders/__init__.py exports Order, next_state, retry_delay and the four error classes. All times are plain numbers measured in minutes. states.py defines: INITIAL = "awaiting_payment"; EVENTS = ("pay", "pay_fail", "pack", "ship", "deliver", "cancel", "return", "refund"); TERMINAL = frozenset of "cancelled" and "refunded"; the dict TRANSITIONS mapping (state, event) to the next state with exactly these entries: (awaiting_payment, pay) -> paid; (awaiting_payment, pay_fail) -> awaiting_payment; (awaiting_payment, cancel) -> cancelled; (paid, pack) -> packed; (paid, cancel) -> refunded; (packed, ship) -> shipped; (packed, cancel) -> refunded; (shipped, deliver) -> delivered; (delivered, return) -> returned; (returned, refund) -> refunded; the constants MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3, RETRY_BASE = 5, RETRY_CAP = 60, RETURN_WINDOW = 20160 (14 days); next_state(state, event), which returns the next state or None when the pair is not in TRANSITIONS; and retry_delay(attempts), the number of minutes to wait after that many failed payments: RETRY_BASE doubled for every failure after the first and never more than RETRY_CAP (5, 10, 20, 40, 60, 60, ...). retry_delay raises TypeError when attempts is not an int (a bool is not accepted) and ValueError when it is below 1. Order(order_id, max_attempts=MAX_ATTEMPTS): order_id must be a str and max_attempts an int that is not a bool (TypeError otherwise), and max_attempts must be at least 1 (ValueError). A new order has the public attributes order_id, state = INITIAL, attempts = 0 (number of failed payments so far), retry_at = None and delivered_at = None, and an empty history. The read-only property history returns a new list of tuples (at, event, from_state, to_state), one per accepted event in order, and the read-only property finished is True exactly when the state is in TERMINAL. order.apply(event, at) tries to apply an event that happened at time at, and returns the new state when it is accepted. Checks are made in this order and the first failure is raised: (1) event must be a str (TypeError) and one of EVENTS (ValueError); (2) at must be an int or float that is not a bool (TypeError) and finite (ValueError); (3) at must not be earlier than the time of the last accepted event (ValueError; equal times are fine, and the very first event may happen at any time, including a negative one); (4) the pair (state, event) must be in TRANSITIONS, otherwise InvalidTransition(state, event) is raised, which also covers every event in a terminal state; (5) a pay or pay_fail event is rejected with RetryTooEarly(retry_at) when order.retry_at is not None and at is earlier than it; every other event, cancel included, is unaffected by retry_at; (6) a return event is rejected with ReturnWindowClosed(deadline) when at is later than delivered_at + RETURN_WINDOW, the deadline being that sum, so a return at exactly the deadline is accepted. A rejected event leaves the order exactly as it was before the call. An accepted event is handled as follows. pay_fail increases attempts by one; if attempts is then at least max_attempts the order goes to "cancelled" and retry_at becomes None, otherwise the state stays awaiting_payment and retry_at becomes at + retry_delay(attempts). pay sets retry_at to None (attempts keeps its value). deliver sets delivered_at to at. All other events just move the order to the state given by TRANSITIONS. The accepted event is appended to the history with the state before and the state after it (for a pay_fail that exhausts the retries the state after is "cancelled").
